To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RuvABC‐dependent DSBs in cells deficient for either the accessory replicative protein Rep or for the main replicative helicases DnaB are formed in different ways: in the case of rep mutants, RuvABC breaks are formed in the absence of RecA, while in the case of dnaBts mutants most of the RUVABC breaks depend on RecA.
RuvABC‐dependent DSBs are made by resolution in the absence of RecA in rep mutants but require RecA in the absence of DnaB, suggesting that RecA acts to form Holliday junctions in the latter case.

RuvABC‐dependent DSBs are induced by replication fork arrest, and that the induction of DSBs by fork arrest depends on RecA in cells with a blocked replicative helicases, but not in cells with an accessory replicative helices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of replication fork breakage in E. coli and its implications in the maintenance of genome stability.
the mechanism of replication fork arrest, and we have identified a novel role for RecA in the resolution of replication intermediates formed at blocked forks.
the mechanisms by which replication forks blocked by the absence of the replicative helicases are repaired.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RecA is required for RuvC‐dependent DSBs at stalled replication forks.
the RuvABC resolvase can act in the absence of any known presynaptic recombination function.

the RecA‐dependent and ‐independent pathways of RuvABC‐dependent DSBs in rep mutants and in dnaBts cells, respectively, represent two alternative ways of processing the stalled replication fork, which are used in different circumstances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in rep cells, the absence of the accessory replicative DNA helicase Rep allows RuvABC‐dependent breakage to occur in the absence of RecA, but in dnaBts cells, the inactivation of the main replicative DNA helix‐unwinding enzyme DnaB causes RuvABC‐induced breakage to depend on RecA.
RuvABC‐dependent DSBs are induced by the inactivation in vivo of the accessory helicase Rep and by the inactivation or depletion of DnaB, and that the latter event requires RecA.
, in rep mutants, replication fork arrest is sufficient to cause DSBs, whereas, in dnaB mutants, the formation of Hollidays junctions and their subsequent resolution requires additional factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RuvABC resolvase is responsible for the breakage of DNA molecules that are arrested at replication forks in E. coli.
the RuvABC resolvase, which is not involved in the repair of DNA damage, is responsible for the formation of DNA DSBs during replication.
the action of RecA in homologous recombined‐mediated double‐strand breakage is more complex than previously thought.
